propositions: One-time backfill script measures cyclomatic complexity (via lizard) and clone count (via jscpd) at sampled historical commits and writes snapshots to the metrics store.
Each backfilled snapshot must be timestamped with the commit's own ISO date (from git), not the wall-clock backfill run time, so trends reflect historical progression.

measure_tree function shells to complexity and clone tools, returning a dict with integer complexity and clone_count; if either tool is absent or errors, measure_tree returns None and that commit is skipped without aborting the backfill.
All written snapshots carry source='snapshot' and confidence='high' metadata tags.

Test suite under tests/scripts/ with pytest.mark.scripts tier mocks measure_tree to avoid external tool dependencies and validates snapshot count, integer-typed metrics, and commit-date timestamp invariant.
